message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1","text":"Peter to James, the lord and bishop of the holy church. May you always be in peace from the Father of all through Jesus Christ. Knowing, my brother, that you eagerly pursue what is beneficial to all of us in common, I ask and implore you not to share with anyone the books of my proclamations that I sent you—not with anyone from the nations, nor with one of our own people before a test—but if someone, after being tested, is found worthy, then to hand them over to him according to the procedure by which Moses also handed them over to the seventy, those who had received his chair. Because of this, the fruit of the safeguard is evident to this day. For those of the same nation everywhere keep the same rule of monarchy and polity, having been unable in any way to be led away into thinking otherwise by Scriptures that point in many directions. For according to the rule handed down to them, they try to rectify the inconsistencies of the Scriptures, if indeed someone who happens not to know the traditions is numbed before the prophets’ many-meaning utterances. For this reason they permit no one to teach unless he first learns how the Scriptures must be used. Therefore among them there is one God, one law, one hope.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἐπισκόπῳ τῆς ἁγίας ἐκκλησίας","chosen":"the lord and bishop of the holy church","rationale":"Here κύριος is an honorific addressed to James rather than a divine title, so lowercase “lord” is used."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐμῶν κηρυγμάτων ἃς ἔπεμψά σοι βίβλους","chosen":"the books of my proclamations that I sent you","rationale":"κηρύγματα denotes proclaimed teachings or messages; “proclamations” preserves its connection with public preaching."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὴν ἀγωγὴν","chosen":"according to the procedure","rationale":"ἀγωγή can denote a manner of conduct, training, or prescribed process; the context concerns the controlled process for transmitting the books."},{"source_quote":"τὸν αὐτὸν ... τῆς μοναρχίας καὶ πολιτείας φυλάσσουσι κανόνα","chosen":"keep the same rule of monarchy and polity","rationale":"The rendering retains both the one-rule language of μοναρχία and the communal or constitutional sense of πολιτεία without harmonizing them."},{"source_quote":"τῶν πολλὰ νευουσῶν γραφῶν","chosen":"Scriptures that point in many directions","rationale":"The image of νεύω is of indicating or gesturing, while πολλά suggests a plurality of apparent directions."},{"source_quote":"τὰς τῶν προφητῶν πολυσήμους φωνάς","chosen":"the prophets’ many-meaning utterances","rationale":"πολύσημος describes language capable of bearing multiple meanings or indications; the deliberately unusual force is retained."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2","text":"So that, then, the same may happen among us as well, give the books of my proclamations to our seventy brothers together with the same mystery of the procedure, so that they too may equip those who wish to undertake a share in the teaching, to equip others. For if this does not happen in this way, our word of truth will be divided into many opinions. I know this not because I am a prophet, but because I already see the beginning of the evil itself. For some of those from the nations have rejected the lawful proclamation delivered through me, having embraced a certain lawless and babbling teaching of the hostile man. And even while I am still alive, some have attempted, through various interpretations, to reshape my words into the abolition of the law, as though even I myself thought in this way but did not proclaim it openly. May such a thing be far away! For such conduct is to oppose the law of God, which was spoken through Moses and attested by our Lord. On its eternal continuance. For he spoke as follows: “Heaven and earth will pass away; one iota or one stroke will certainly not pass away from the law.” And he said this: “before all things happen.” But they—I do not know how—claiming to know my mind, attempt to interpret the words they heard from me more intelligently than I, the one who spoke them, telling those being instructed by them that this is my way of thinking, though I never even conceived it. But if, while I am still alive, they dare to tell such lies about me, how much more, after me, will those who come after me dare to do so?","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μετὰ τοῦ ὁμοίου τῆς ἀγωγῆς μυστηρίου","chosen":"together with the same mystery of the procedure","rationale":"μυστήριον retains the secrecy or solemn rite associated with the prescribed process of transmission; the Greek does not specify its exact form here."},{"source_quote":"τὸ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ νόμιμον ... κήρυγμα","chosen":"the lawful proclamation delivered through me","rationale":"νόμιμος is rendered “lawful” because the immediate contrast is with ἄνομος and with the alleged abolition of the law."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἐχθροῦ ἀνθρώπου","chosen":"the hostile man","rationale":"The wording identifies an antagonistic man without naming him; the translation does not import a proposed historical identity."},{"source_quote":"φλυαρώδη ... διδασκαλίαν","chosen":"babbling teaching","rationale":"φλύαρος conveys empty, nonsensical, or rambling talk rather than merely an incorrect opinion."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς ἀιδίου αὐτοῦ διαμονῆς","chosen":"On its eternal continuance","rationale":"The supplied punctuation isolates the phrase, so it is retained as a heading-like fragment; αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to the law."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἐμὸν νοῦν ἐπαγγελλόμενοι","chosen":"claiming to know my mind","rationale":"ἐπαγγέλλομαι here expresses professing or claiming competence concerning Peter’s intended meaning."},{"source_quote":"ἐμοῦ τοῦ εἰπόντος αὐτοὺς φρονιμώτερον","chosen":"more intelligently than I, the one who spoke them","rationale":"The comparative force is preserved: the interpreters claim greater insight into the sayings than their speaker possesses."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐφοδιάζειν ἐφοδιάζωσιν","issue":"The independently checked selected print contains both the infinitive and the adjacent finite form. Their repetition produces a compressed and syntactically uncertain construction. The translation preserves both as “equip ... to equip”; possible dittography remains conjectural.","proposed_reading":"ἵνα καὶ τοὺς βουλομένους τὸ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἀναδέξασθαι μέρος ἐφοδιάζωσιν","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"πρὶν ἂν τὰ πάντα γίνεται","issue":"The indicative γίνεται is irregular after πρὶν ἄν, where a subjunctive would ordinarily be expected. The supplied reading is retained as the source, while the English necessarily gives the clause’s apparent sense.","proposed_reading":"πρὶν ἂν τὰ πάντα γένηται","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"3","text":"So that nothing of this sort may happen, for this reason I asked and implored you not to share with anyone the books of my proclamations that I sent you—neither with one of our own people nor with one of another people before a test—but if someone, after being tested, is found worthy, then to hand them over to him according to Moses’ procedure, by which he handed them over to the seventy, those who had received his chair, so that in this way they may keep the pledges and everywhere hand on the rule of truth, interpreting everything in accordance with our tradition, and may not themselves, dragged downward by ignorance and drawn into error by conjectures within the soul, carry others into the same pit of destruction. And I have duly indicated to you the things that seemed good to me; as for what seems good to you, my lord, carry it out fittingly. Farewell.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μήτε ὁμοφύλῳ μήτε ἀλλοφύλῳ","chosen":"neither with one of our own people nor with one of another people","rationale":"The paired terms distinguish someone of the same people or stock from someone of a different people without supplying a more specific ethnic identity."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὴν Μωϋσέως ἀγωγὴν","chosen":"according to Moses’ procedure","rationale":"As in the preceding passages, ἀγωγή refers to the prescribed process governing transmission of the books."},{"source_quote":"τὰς πίστεις φυλάξωσιν","chosen":"keep the pledges","rationale":"The plural πίστεις can denote assurances, commitments, or pledges; “pledges” preserves the plural and suits the controlled transmission context."},{"source_quote":"τῶν κατὰ τὴν ψυχὴν στοχασμῶν","chosen":"conjectures within the soul","rationale":"στοχασμοί are speculative inferences or conjectures, here located in the inner life rather than in the received tradition."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ὅμοιον τῆς ἀπωλείας ... βόθυνον","chosen":"the same pit of destruction","rationale":"The rendering preserves the source’s image of error ending in a destructive pit."},{"source_quote":"ἔρρωσο","chosen":"Farewell","rationale":"Although literally an exhortation to be strong or well, this is the conventional singular epistolary closing."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
